role: Sr. Business Intelligence Engineer, AWS Marketplace
responsibilities: Owning complex, ambiguous analytical problems end to end, from the underlying data models through the insights that inform leadership decisions
Owning analytics for high-visibility, VP-tracked launches: telemetry design, attribution methodology, day-one metrics, and post-launch funnel analysis
Building standardized, reusable reporting infrastructure so onboarding a new launch is a configuration change, not weeks of custom work
Designing trusted, secure data foundations (metric layers, data dictionaries, and a semantic layer) that power agentic analytics
Leading strategic deep dives on loosely defined questions and delivering leadership-ready narratives with a recommended path forward
Influencing product and engineering on upstream data requirements so data is analytics-ready by design
Authoring leadership-facing narratives and presenting insights directly to senior stakeholders
Mentoring junior BIEs and codifying analytical patterns into standards the team adopts

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Designing trusted, secure data foundations (metric layers, data dictionaries, and a semantic layer) that power agentic analytics
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Trusted, secure, standardised foundations and standards carry the posting, with no speed phrases.
evidence.domain_risk: own analytics end to end for the Marketplace's highest-visibility product launches
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Product-launch analytics affects leadership decisions without regulatory or financial-reporting language, so it is moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: You'll join the Product Analytics team, the trusted business partner and subject-matter expert
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A product analytics team inside a large AWS organisation, with junior BIEs to mentor, is an established function at scale.
evidence.jd_authorship: Owning analytics for high-visibility, VP-tracked launches: telemetry design, attribution methodology, day-one metrics, and post-launch funnel analysis
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name telemetry design, attribution, metric layers and a semantic layer in context, so a reader knows the day-to-day work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: telemetry design, attribution methodology, day-one metrics, and post-launch funnel analysis
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Product launches, funnels and product-engineering partners place the emphasis on product.
evidence.autonomy_level: You'll drive the shift toward prescriptive analytics that shapes organizational strategy, and set the technical and analytical standards the team builds on.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns problems end to end, leads deep dives and sets team standards.
evidence.ai_role: Designing trusted, secure data foundations (metric layers, data dictionaries, and a semantic layer) that power agentic analytics
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the semantic layer and foundations that agentic tooling consumes, so it is ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: No testing or data-quality practice is named; "trusted" foundations are described without a testing mechanism.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: build the trusted, reusable data foundations
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust is named but secondary to delivering launch analytics, so it is moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Building standardized, reusable reporting infrastructure so onboarding a new launch is a configuration change
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: New reusable infrastructure is built inside an existing analytics team.
evidence.loss_aversion: trusted, reusable data foundations — secondary to delivery.
